summary: LND: a malformed DNS seed response can crash the node
details: lnd's DNS peer bootstrapper, on by default on mainnet, falls back to a TCP lookup when the first query fails. That fallback assumed every answer record was of one type, so any other record type caused an unhandled panic that stopped the daemon. An attacker on the network path, or a malicious or compromised DNS seed operator, can trigger it whenever the node looks for peers (at startup or when it has too few peers). No funds are at risk and the node restarts cleanly. Fixed in 0.21.1-beta (released 2026-06-30) and 0.20.2-beta (released 2026-07-08). Operators who cannot update can set nobootstrap=true. Disclosed 2026-09-21, tier T3; no CVE listed.

database_specific.range_note: introduced version is not stated by the source; 0 is a placeholder meaning 'unknown start'. The 0.21.0-beta start is a structural placeholder for the second fixed line.

conditions.note: DNS bootstrapping is on by default on mainnet; nobootstrap=true avoids the bug
regtest has no DNS seeds, so the bootstrapper never runs there; signet is kept on the affected side because the source does not say whether it has seeds

playbook: Check the LND version and whether nobootstrap=true is set in lnd.conf.
Update to 0.20.2-beta (0.20 line) or 0.21.1-beta (0.21 line) or newer.
If you cannot update yet, set nobootstrap=true and restart, then remove it after updating if you rely on DNS seeds.
